notes: Skill 29/29 assertions (100%); baseline 19/29 (65.5%). The gap is entirely structural, not informational.

NON-DISCRIMINATING: 'no new tool calls' and the line-count ceilings passed 6/6. Sonnet never re-investigated and never over-wrote, with or without the skill — these assertions are currently free points and should be replaced or made harsher next iteration.

Every baseline failure is one of two kinds: (a) no fixed scaffold — each run invented a different shape (Task/Root cause/Fix; Problem/Fix/Verified; bolded workstream paragraphs), so a reader gets no predictable place to look; (b) dropped file:line references — 0 of 3 baselines kept a line number, 3 of 3 skill runs did.

The other recurring baseline failure is bottom-line placement: eval-0 opens on the topic ('Task: Investigate flaky checkout tests') and eval-2 buries the sentence that names both blockers in a closing 'Bottom line' paragraph. The skill's TL;DR-first rule fixes exactly this.

Content fidelity was strong in BOTH configurations — hedges survived, bad news survived, tradeoffs survived. Sonnet is already good at faithful summarising; the skill is not buying accuracy here, it is buying consistency and scannability. Worth being honest about that.
Cost of the skill: +2.2s (18.9s vs 17.6s) and +2.5k tokens per call. Small, but it is the price of loading SKILL.md.

QUALITATIVE WATCH ITEM: the eval-2 skill TL;DR is a single 48-word sentence packing four separate items. The baseline's bolded per-workstream sections were more scannable at session scale. The skill may need explicit guidance on splitting the TL;DR, or on sub-grouping Did/Found by workstream when the session is long.
Single run per configuration — no variance data. Treat the 100% as directional, not settled.
